new_higher_level_source.authors: Vili-Taneli Salo, Jing Chen, Nino Runeberg, Henrik G. Kjaergaard, Theo Kurten
new_higher_level_source.title: Multireference and Coupled-Cluster Study of Dimethyltetroxide (MeO4Me) Formation and Decomposition

scientific_update.method: CASPT2(22e,14o)-IPEA(0.20)/cc-pVTZ with multireference methodology benchmarked against CCSD(T)/CBS, W2X, and W3X-L relative energies
scientific_update.source_statement: The 2024 study reports that at its preferred CASPT2(22e,14o)-IPEA/cc-pVTZ description, both dimethyltetroxide formation and decomposition follow minimum-energy pathways without saddle points; possible transition states and pre/postreaction complexes are strongly method dependent.

quantity_typing.typing_note: These are relative electronic energies between separated species and the tetroxide minimum. They are reaction energetics, not activation barriers, not DeltaG-dagger values, and not Arrhenius activation energies.

scientific_update.relation_to_2022_profile: The 2022 CASSCF profile contained small formation/decomposition saddle points, while the 2024 higher-level follow-up finds that those stationary-point features are not robust to the improved multireference treatment. The earlier numerical CASSCF barriers remain valid provenance records for that method but are not licensed as a unique physical single-barrier coordinate for the MeO2 self-reaction.
scientific_update.selection_independence_note: The 2024 preferred multireference method is selected by agreement with coupled-cluster theoretical benchmarks of relative energies, not by residual agreement with the Onel experimental target. This makes the topology result scientifically relevant without using experimental-rate agreement as a selector.

barrier_gate_basis: A single barrier height cannot be assigned merely by choosing one of the 2022 CASSCF/XMC-QDPT2 saddle-point values after the higher-level 2024 surface removes those saddle points.
The 14.99 kcal/mol reactant-to-tetroxide relative electronic energy is an exothermicity magnitude relative to the tetroxide reference, not an activation barrier.

The 22.88 kcal/mol tetroxide-to-separated-product relative electronic energy is reaction energetics and cannot be relabeled as a decomposition activation barrier when the preferred minimum-energy pathway has no saddle point.

Any future kinetic coordinate must be defined through an explicitly registered network bottleneck, capture/association free-energy bottleneck, variational transition state, or other rate-controlling quantity whose physical mapping is independently justified.
decision_required: Do not choose between the 2022 saddle-point profile and the 2024 barrierless preferred topology by observed-rate agreement. The campaign must either reconstruct an independently specified network/capture-rate model consistent with the higher-level topology or locate a different MC16 family with a robust independently typed kinetic bottleneck.
next_gate: Continue attempting to recover and audit 2022 SI Section S5/Table S5 solely to classify the published MESMER result as independent prediction versus calibration; that audit cannot restore a single-saddle-point barrier if the preferred higher-level PES is barrierless.

Search for a prospectively or methodologically independent variational/capture/master-equation treatment of MeO2 + MeO2 that reports the exact 295 K and pressure/bath-gas mapping without selecting model parameters by the Onel target.
In parallel, continue MC16 family search outward so methylperoxy need not be forced through the Atlas if its physically correct representation cannot satisfy the barrier-rate coordinate requirements.
Keep quantitative branching as a separate unresolved network gate.
